defectsFoundThisSession.summary: RECOVERY_PLAN.md section 6 verified a restored database with 'expect 45 tables, 47 procedures' and five named suites. The schema is 84 and 102, with twenty suites.
defectsFoundThisSession.whyItMattered: A backup taken before ten feature schemas existed matches 45/47 EXACTLY, so the gate reports a clean verification of a catastrophically incomplete restore - during an incident, to somebody deciding whether to return it to service. Demonstrated: a real database on the instance is still 45/47 and fails 15 of 21 checks under the new drill.
defectsFoundThisSession.fix: Section 6 is now ops/db/restore-drill.sh, which enumerates suites from disk and checks behaviour rather than shape. The old commands also omitted -S and had never been run as written.
defectsFoundThisSession.foundBy: parallel operational audit, verified against the live instance

defectsFoundThisSession.summary: The apply loop in README, CLAUDE.md, PLATFORM_RUNBOOK and both CI jobs ended '|| break' but omitted sqlcmd -b, so sqlcmd exited 0 on a T-SQL error and the break was dead code.
defectsFoundThisSession.whyItMattered: A failure at script 34 did not stop anything: the loop ran the rest against a broken database and finished looking like success. Same class as the audit-contract ordering bug and the twice-repeated silently-green CI step - a guard that cannot fire.
defectsFoundThisSession.fix: -b added in all four copies; ops/db/deploy.sh supersedes them; ci_workflow_test.sh now fails if any schema-application line in CI omits -b.

defectsFoundThisSession.summary: .dockerignore excluded neither appsettings.Development.json nor .env, so the committed development JWT signing key was copied into every image built.
defectsFoundThisSession.whyItMattered: The runtime sets ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production so the file is not read - but anyone who can read the image layers can read the key, and setting the environment to Development on a production container would activate it. A secret that ships is a secret that leaked.
defectsFoundThisSession.fix: .dockerignore now excludes development appsettings, .env files and backup artefacts. The startup guard requiring a 32-character signing key already existed and was verified working: the API refuses to boot in Production without one.
defectsFoundThisSession.foundBy: parallel operational audit; the startup guard confirmed by running the API as Production

defectsFoundThisSession.summary: Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK ran 'dotnet Maren.Api.dll --healthcheck'; Program.cs never inspected args, so the probe started a second full web host that could not bind the port and exited non-zero. The compose override that supposedly masked it shelled out to wget, which the aspnet runtime image does not contain.
defectsFoundThisSession.whyItMattered: The container reported unhealthy forever while serving traffic correctly. The prior ledger entry said 'would restart-loop', which overstates it: plain Docker Engine only marks a container unhealthy. A restart loop needs an orchestrator; under plain docker run the effect is a load balancer refusing to route to a healthy instance.
defectsFoundThisSession.fix: HealthProbe implemented in Maren.Api and returned from Program.cs before any host is built; compose now uses the same probe. Verified locally by exit code only - NO DOCKER on this machine, so it has never run inside a container.
defectsFoundThisSession.foundBy: reading Program.cs for the argument, confirmed by the parallel audit

defectsFoundThisSession.summary: ci_workflow_test.sh — the guard against a silently-green CI step — was never invoked by any CI job.
defectsFoundThisSession.whyItMattered: The same class of defect it exists to catch. Nothing enforced the invariant it protects.
defectsFoundThisSession.fix: Added as a CI step, and the guard now asserts its own presence in the workflow. It also gained checks that every schema script is applied in CI and that schema application uses -b.

defectsFoundThisSession.summary: The first draft of the ops append-only assertion searched sys.sql_modules for '%UPDATE%[Ops].[DeploymentJournal]%'. Square brackets in a T-SQL LIKE pattern are a character class, so this asked for 'UPDATE then any one of O/p/s' and reported eight offenders that did not exist.
defectsFoundThisSession.whyItMattered: A guard that fires on nothing real trains people to ignore it. It failed loudly on first run rather than silently passing, which is the better direction to fail.
defectsFoundThisSession.fix: Resolved through sys.sql_expression_dependencies instead: which procedures reference an Ops journal at all, and do any contain a mutating verb. Mutation-tested.

defectsFoundThisSession.summary: Predict.Predicted (SubjectKey) and Predict.PredictionType (HorizonCode) were created with foreign keys and no supporting index.
defectsFoundThisSession.whyItMattered: Predicted grows once per woman per prediction per day. The parent-side delete and every join to Behaviour.Subject would have scanned the one new table with real cardinality.
defectsFoundThisSession.fix: Guarded IF NOT EXISTS ... CREATE INDEX outside the CREATE TABLE block, following 30_Indexes_ForeignKeys.sql. Inside the block the index would never reach a database that already had the table, so re-applying would not converge - the same shape as the audit contract defect.
defectsFoundThisSession.foundBy: index_coverage_test.sql on the clean-room run, not by the 20 assertions written for this feature

defectsFoundThisSession.summary: T-SQL ROUND rounds half away from zero; .NET Math.Round uses banker's rounding. An observed 0.325 is 33% on the server and 32% in .NET.
defectsFoundThisSession.whyItMattered: Caught by an integration test written against .NET's default. Not a server defect - but a client that recomputed the percent instead of using the shipped one would show a woman a different number from the one in her own statement text.
defectsFoundThisSession.fix: The percent is computed once, server-side, and shipped. The test now asserts MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero to match the server on purpose, with the reason recorded beside it.
defectsFoundThisSession.foundBy: the integration test failing on its first run

architecturalInvariants: Ops.RestoreDrill will not store a passing drill that ran no checks, or one with any failing check. A CHECK constraint refuses it, because 'RESTORE returned 0' is not evidence that a database was restored. Restore verification checks BEHAVIOUR - DBCC CHECKDB plus every assertion suite on disk - never counts of tables or procedures, which go stale silently and once would have passed a database missing ten feature schemas.
Both Ops journals are append-only, asserted through the dependency graph rather than module text: no procedure that references them may contain a mutating verb.
There is ONE deployment order and it lives in docs/PLATFORM_RUNBOOK.md. ops/db/deploy.sh reads it rather than carrying a copy, and asserts the documented count against the scripts on disk.

Predict.fn_PredictFrom is the ONLY framing logic, and it cannot compute. A PredictionType carries a SourceFamily pinned to 'probability' by a CHECK, and (SourceMeasureCode, SourceFamily) is a foreign key into Behaviour.MeasureType (MeasureCode, Family) — so a prediction may only name a measure Behaviour publishes as a probability. A CHECK refuses a framing missing {chance}, {window} or {support}, so no configuration can state a likelihood without its window and its support.

Coach.fn_ExplainFrom is the ONLY explanation logic. A message is filled into a tone pattern; a CHECK constraint refuses a pattern missing {body} or {reason}, so no configuration can encourage without evidence. The coach never reassembles.
Recommend.fn_AssembleFrom is the ONLY assembly logic. It consumes an EvidenceSet and reads no raw store — verified by dependency graph. The live path and the Decision Inspector both feed it.

Behaviour.fn_Measure is the ONLY copy of the measure arithmetic. It consumes a DaySet and an HourSet and reads no per-user source — verified by dependency graph, not by text. The real observer and the Decision Inspector both feed it.
Behaviour.fn_Observe is the only computation of behaviour. Consumption goes through Behaviour.fn_Read and Behaviour.fn_ReadSteps.
Growth.Routine NEVER owns a step list. It references Behaviour.Subject. Asserted structurally: no Step/EventType/Percent column may exist on Growth.Routine.
Routine completion is derived from logged events every time. No stored percentage, no mark-complete command, no completion endpoint. Asserted at the contract boundary too.
Goal achievement is earned from the timeline, forward-only, and refused to clients by validator and procedure.
Applicability for content, dashboard cards, goals and routines all go through Rules.fn_Match. One matcher.

Reminder timing is deliberately NOT a prediction. Behaviour already observes preferred_hour; restating an observation in the future tense would be a rename, and the foreign key above cannot express it because a preference is not a probability.
